# About · Panda Federation

Source: https://pandafederation.com/about.html

# About Panda Federation

## A dad, a shared computer, and a team of bots

Panda Federation is one dad's workshop. I build public-data tools with a small team of AI bots that share one computer. One bot writes and tests code, another checks listings and links, another keeps the books and the calendar honest, and I decide what ships.

The bots don't run on trust. Every tool they build is tested against the official source it reads (Crossref, SAM.gov, the NPI Registry, state business filings, RDAP and others) before it goes public. Every listing is checked against the live store page. When a bot finds a page that hides instructions aimed at AI agents, it logs the page and doesn't follow them. That habit became a tool: the [Hidden AI Instructions Scanner](https://apify.com/pandadad0214/hidden-ai-instructions-scanner).

## What we build

- **Public-data tools for AI agents.** Apify Actors and MCP servers that pull from official sources: reference checks, federal grants and bids, official lead lists, domain and email security. ([Apify tools](apify.html) · [MCP servers](mcp.html))
- **Local-first tools for bot teams.** [Quiet File Team](quiet-file-team/) is the plain-file system our own bots use to share one computer: a task queue, short handoff notes, and an early exit so idle routines stop instead of spending tokens. [Steel Panda](https://github.com/pandadad0214/Steel_Panda) and [Watchdog Panda](https://github.com/pandadad0214/Watchdog_Panda) are the small shell tools that keep it running.
- **Free guides.** The [data broker removal guide](data-broker-removal/) grew out of our own opt-out work and became a page anyone can use.

## How we work

- **Official sources only.** If a tool can't name its source, it doesn't ship.
- **Free and paid editions always name each other.** When a tool has a free version and a paid one, both pages say so and explain how to switch. List rates on this site are rebuilt from the Apify Store API and shown on each Apify tool card and on [pricing.md](pricing.md). The Store page is authoritative. Fiverr, Upwork and Agensi package prices stay on those listings.
- **No invented numbers.** Counts on this site rebuild themselves from the Apify Store, PyPI and GitHub, and the sample tables come from real runs.
- **Built slow, built steady.** At most one new tool a day, and only once it works.

## Contact

The public contact paths are GitHub and X only. There is no personal email or phone on this site. [GitHub](https://github.com/pandadad0214) · [Follow on X: @PandaFedHQ](https://x.com/PandaFedHQ)

This website is the public catalog for the Federation. The official site is [https://pandafederation.com/](https://pandafederation.com/). Hardware (cables, racks, and lab gear) is sold separately at [Panda Federation Shop](https://shop.pandafederation.com/); that catalog is assigned independently, so the shop may show no products yet.

# Free Data Broker Removal Guide + State Law Map · Panda Federation

Source: https://pandafederation.com/data-broker-removal/

**Not legal advice. This page is a research guide built from official sources and the sites' own pages, checked on the date shown. It does not apply any law to your situation. For advice, talk to a licensed attorney in your state.**

Panda Federation does not submit forms for you, does not ask for your personal details, and is not paid by any site listed here. You open every link and fill every form yourself.
[Steps](#steps)[Pitfalls](#pitfalls)[Opt-out links](#sites)[State law map](#state-map)[Checklist](#checklist)[State map JSON](state-law-map.json)[Links JSON](optout-sites.json)

## Order of steps

- **Inventory first.** List the emails, phone numbers and old accounts you still control. Search each inbox for sign-up and marketing mail to find forgotten accounts.
- **Delete old accounts while you can still sign in.** Some sites only accept deletion from a signed-in session. Finish those before you close the email address that gets their codes.
- **Find your listings and confirm they are you.** Common names pull up other people. Only opt out of a record that is actually yours.
- **Opt out at the official link, in your own browser.** Use the links below. Captchas often fail in automated or remote browsers, so open them yourself.
- **Click verification emails right away.** Links commonly expire in 24 hours, and some much sooner. One in our testing expired in about 15 minutes.
- **Save the receipt.** Keep the confirmation email or screenshot. Log the result from that message, not from memory. A reply that says denied is easy to misread as done.
- **Recheck later.** Look again after the window the site gives (often 3 days), then every month or two. Listings can come back when new public records arrive.

## Pitfalls

- Never pay a people-search site to remove you. Their opt-outs are free.
- Delete linked accounts before you delete an old email address.
- Where you live matters. Many sites only grant formal privacy rights to residents of states with a comprehensive privacy law. Everyone else gets a courtesy opt-out, if that.
- Most state laws exclude publicly available information, such as government records. That is what many listings are built from, so a legal deletion right may not force a takedown.
- Do not misstate your state of residence on a form.
- If an account-deletion email tells you not to sign back in, don't. Signing in can cancel the deletion on some sites.

## Official opt-out links

Checked November 10, 2026. “Bot check” means our automated check hit a captcha or firewall. The address is still the site's own opt-out path, so open it in your own browser.

### Rights depend on your state

SmartBackgroundChecks, USPhonebook and FastPeopleSearch publish near-identical privacy notices. They say your privacy rights depend on your state of residence and point residents of states with comprehensive privacy laws to a supplemental notice. They take requests through a web form or by phone. They also say their data is publicly available information, which they consider outside state privacy laws, and that they apply opt-outs to it as a courtesy. If you live in a state without a comprehensive law, such as Arizona, expect a formal privacy request to be refused. The opt-out form is still worth trying.
SiteOfficial linkStatusNotesSmartBackgroundChecks[www.smartbackgroundchecks.com/optout](https://www.smartbackgroundchecks.com/optout)LoadedEmailed form link expires in 24 hours. Allow 3 days. Privacy rights depend on your state of residence. ## State law map: who has a legal right to deletion

**19 states** have a comprehensive privacy law in effect with a right to delete. Florida's narrow law adds a deletion right that reaches only very large companies. Oklahoma and Louisiana start January 1, 2027, Alabama May 1, 2027, and Vermont January 1, 2028. California's free [DROP](https://consumer.drop.privacy.ca.gov/) tool sends one deletion request to registered data brokers, for California residents only.

**The catch:** most of these laws exclude publicly available information, such as government records, from the data they cover. People-search listings are largely built from those records, so a deletion right may not force a takedown. Sites often apply opt-outs to that data only as a courtesy.

### Arizona

Arizona has no comprehensive consumer privacy law, so Arizona residents have no general legal right to make a people-search site delete a listing. The Arizona Attorney General's consumer pages cover data-breach notice, not deletion, and SB 1815 (2026) was only introduced. Arizona residents can still use each site's free opt-out form. Many sites honor those as a courtesy. Sites that tie formal rights to state law may refuse.

Arkansas: we found no enacted comprehensive privacy law. Some sites cite “Act 549 of 2023,” but the [official Act 549](https://arkleg.state.ar.us/Acts/FTPDocument?ddBienniumSession=2023/2023R&file=549.pdf&path=%2FACTS%2F2023R%2FPublic%2F) is a firearms bill.

# Digest #1: Server Actors, a release calendar for MCP, and an SEC deadline · Panda Federation

Source: https://pandafederation.com/digest/001-2026-11-12/

Digest #1 · 2026-11-12

# Server Actors, a release calendar for MCP, and an SEC deadline

Five things from the last few days that matter if your agent works with public data, with our take on each, and then what we shipped.

## MCP gets a release calendar (Nov 11)

The MCP maintainers are moving spec releases to a fixed six-month schedule, on the last Tuesday of March and September. The next one is targeted for March 30, 2027. A proposal that isn't ready moves to the next release instead of holding up the spec. **Our take:** this is the most useful MCP news of the week for small server authors. We can plan our server updates around two known dates instead of watching the spec repo. [Read the post](https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/mcp-release-cycle/)

## File uploads and downloads are coming to MCP, as an experiment (Nov 10)

An optional extension, `io.modelcontextprotocol/files`, would let clients and tools move files in and out of band. It's explicitly experimental, has no reference implementation yet, and the maintainers hope to stabilize it before the end of the year. **Our take:** PDF table extraction and Excel exports are the clumsiest part of agent data work today, so a standard way to hand a file to a tool would help a lot. We won't build on it until it reaches Beta. [Read the post](https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/exploring-file-uploads-and-downloads-in-mcp/)

## Apify makes Server Actors generally available (Nov 10)

At its Run by Apify event, Apify announced general availability of Server Actors: always-ready services that answer requests like an API, without starting a new run for each call. Apify AI also gained the ability to orchestrate several Actors and build new ones from plain-language instructions. **Our take:** for agent tool calls, start-up time matters as much as the data does. Quick lookups such as a single domain check or one VIN are the obvious first candidates for an always-on version. [Read the announcement](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/11/10/3399579/0/en/apify-unveils-new-ai-agent-capabilities-and-server-actors-to-support-growing-demand.html)

## Apify MCP server 0.21.5 and 0.21.6 (Nov 10–11)

Two quick releases. 0.21.5 lists only dataset field selections that actually work and explains empty or past-the-end dataset pages. 0.21.6 identifies MCP-server Actors in Actor details. **Our take:** small fixes, but they target a real failure mode. Agents that page past the end of a dataset and read the empty page as "no results" give wrong answers. [Release notes](https://github.com/apify/apify-mcp-server/releases)

## SEC draft 2027 taxonomies: technical feedback closes Nov 16

The SEC posted its draft 2027 taxonomy update on Sept. 14 and is taking technical feedback until 4 p.m. ET on Nov. 16, 2026. It's a draft for comment, not an approved change. **Our take:** anyone who pulls XBRL facts from EDGAR, including our SEC Financials Actor, should read the release notes now, before element changes show up in real filings. [SEC notice](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/whats-new/260914-draft-2027-sec-taxonomies)

## What we shipped

- [Quiet File Team MCP 0.1.1](https://pypi.org/project/quiet-file-team-mcp/) is on PyPI and the Official MCP Registry. Install with `uvx quiet-file-team-mcp`.
- [SAM.gov Contract Opportunities](https://apify.com/pandadad0214/sam-gov-opportunities) is a new Actor that finds open federal bids from the official public data extract, with no API key.
- The four focused MCP servers reached v0.2.0, and the umbrella package reached v1.8.0 ([all servers](https://pandafederation.com/mcp.html)).
- The [free data broker removal guide + state law map](https://pandafederation.com/data-broker-removal/) has opt-out links checked November 10, 2026.
- The site now has a [What's New](https://pandafederation.com/whats-new/) changelog with an Atom feed, plus real sample output on the homepage.

[All issues](../) · [What's New](../../whats-new/)

# Quiet File Team MCP · Panda Federation

Source: https://pandafederation.com/quiet-file-team-mcp/

Quiet File Team MCP gives Claude, Cursor or any MCP client six offline tools that explain, configure and check a Quiet File Team — several bots sharing one computer through files. Nothing leaves your machine: no network calls, no file reads of your disk, no paid APIs.

Use it with the free [Bash core](../quiet-file-team/) (scripts on [GitHub](https://github.com/pandadad0214/quiet-file-team)), or with the optional paid [Quiet File Team Setup Kit](https://agensi.io/skills/quiet-file-team-setup-kit) on Agensi when you want a guided install.

## Install

Python 3.11+ and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) on the client. No account or token is required.

```
uvx quiet-file-team-mcp
```

Published on [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/quiet-file-team-mcp/) and listed on the [Official MCP Registry](https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0/servers?search=io.github.pandadad0214/quiet-file-team-mcp) as `io.github.pandadad0214/quiet-file-team-mcp`.

MCP client config:

```
{"mcpServers":{"quiet-file-team":{"command":"uvx","args":["quiet-file-team-mcp"]}}}
```

## Tools
**explain_method**Concepts and trust limits before an exercise.**generate_team_config**Safe roster and zone defaults; lead-only coordinator.**generate_early_exit**Draft a quoted early-exit block for a supplied role/path.**validate_layout_manifest**Compare supplied relative paths (no real filesystem scan).**draft_workflow**Fictional practice steps for the default roster.**draft_owner_batch**Deduplicate owner questions; keep unresolved task refs.

## Switch editions

- **Free MCP companion** — this page. Install with the uvx command above. Source is on [GitHub](https://github.com/pandadad0214/quiet-file-team-mcp).
- **Free Bash core** — product page: [Quiet File Team](../quiet-file-team/). Clone [quiet-file-team](https://github.com/pandadad0214/quiet-file-team), set TEAM_DIR to the checkout, and follow its README. This MCP explains and checks a team; it does not install those scripts.
- **Quiet File Team Setup Kit** — paid Agensi skill, one-time price on the live listing. Guided local install, ready rules, and practice files. [Open Agensi](https://agensi.io/skills/quiet-file-team-setup-kit)
- **Setup kit generator** — paid Apify Actor that builds a configured starter ZIP. List rate is on the Apify Tools card and on [pricing.md](../pricing.md); the Store page is authoritative. [Open Apify Store](https://apify.com/pandadad0214/quiet-file-team-setup)

# Quiet File Team · Panda Federation

Source: https://pandafederation.com/quiet-file-team/

## What it is

Quiet File Team lets several AI bots share one computer through plain files, so idle routines stop on `NO WORK` instead of spending tokens. It is a free, MIT-licensed Bash kit (pair notes, an append-only task queue, a board and an early-exit check) with no server, chat bus or LLM inside.

It runs on one shared Linux machine. It is not a hosted service, not a replacement for the owner’s chat, and not a way for bots to talk behind the owner’s back.
[GitHub repo](https://github.com/pandadad0214/quiet-file-team)[Free MCP companion](../quiet-file-team-mcp/)[Latest release (v0.1.0)](https://github.com/pandadad0214/quiet-file-team/releases/tag/v0.1.0)

## Who it is for

Use it when two or more bots or scheduled routines share one machine and you want idle runs to exit early and handoffs to live in files.

Do not use it when bots run on different machines without a shared local disk, you need authentication or encryption, or you need real-time chat.

## How it works

Each bot’s chat is for the owner. A shared computer plus files is the bus; there are no background listeners or hidden chat channels. Every routine starts with `has-work.sh <id>`. Exactly `NO WORK` means stop: no chat, no status, no board line. Otherwise pick up only the listed work.
**Pair files**`pairs/<a-b>.md` hold short, directed handoffs. Notes over 2000 characters get an overflow file under `pairs/long/`.**Task queue**`tasks.log` is append-only. The latest event for a task is its state: `open`, `claimed`, `done`, `blocked`, `needs-owner`, `decided` or `cancelled`.**Board**`board.md` is an append-only summary, updated via `post.sh`. It is not a transcript.**Early exit**Start every routine with `has-work.sh` and stop when it prints exactly `NO WORK`. It always exits 0, so check the output.

Scripts serialize mutations using `flock`. All writes stay on the local disk: no network, no scheduler, no model calls. Requirements are Linux, Bash 4+, GNU coreutils, awk, sed, tar and util-linux `flock`.

Ids label records; they do not prove identity. This is not authentication, access control or encrypted storage. Never put private data in this bus.

## Install and quick start

Copy the kit into a shared local folder. Keep its scripts and `team.conf` together. No package registry is required.

```
curl -fsSL https://github.com/pandadad0214/quiet-file-team/archive/refs/tags/v0.1.0.tar.gz | tar xz && mv quiet-file-team-0.1.0 team
export TEAM_DIR="$PWD/team"
bash "$TEAM_DIR/has-work.sh" helper # a fresh kit prints: NO WORK
```

Or clone the repo: `git clone https://github.com/pandadad0214/quiet-file-team.git team`.

- Name your bots in `team/team.conf` (`TEAM_IDS="lead builder helper"`) and set `TEAM_TZ` (default `UTC`).
- Start every routine with `bash "$TEAM_DIR/has-work.sh" <id>` and stop the routine when it prints exactly `NO WORK`.
- Give each bot the core rules in the repo and paste the early-exit block into each routine. Then run the practice exercise once in a fresh folder.

A short practice run on an untouched demo log:

```
export TEAM_DIR="$PWD/team"
bash "$TEAM_DIR/task.sh" new lead helper "Sort a sample inbox"
bash "$TEAM_DIR/task.sh" claim T0001 helper
bash "$TEAM_DIR/task.sh" set T0001 done helper "Sample inbox sorted"
bash "$TEAM_DIR/post.sh" helper done "Demo checklist updated"
bash "$TEAM_DIR/pair.sh" lead builder "Review the demo checklist"
bash "$TEAM_DIR/has-work.sh" helper
# NO WORK
```

Use the task id printed by `new` if the folder already contains tasks. Do not run the demo against a production data folder. Full commands and trust limits are in the [GitHub README](https://github.com/pandadad0214/quiet-file-team#how-to-use-this).

## Commands
**has-work.sh <id>**Print pending `TASKS:` / `HANDOFFS:` or exactly `NO WORK`.**task.sh**`new`, `claim`, `set`, `list`, `owner`, `stale`, `show`.**pair.sh**Append a directed pair note; `read [count]` reads recent lines.**post.sh**Append `done`, `needs-owner`, `handoff: <id>`, `fyi` or `resolved`.**backup.sh**Optional local snapshot of board, task log and pairs. No upload.

## Switch editions

The free core on this page is enough to run a team. A free MCP companion explains and checks a layout. A paid setup kit is also live if you want a guided install or a pre-configured ZIP.

- **Free Bash core** — this page. Install with the curl or git clone command above. Source is on [GitHub](https://github.com/pandadad0214/quiet-file-team).
- **Free MCP companion** — six offline guidance tools (explain the method, draft config and early-exit text, validate a supplied layout, draft a practice workflow, batch owner questions). It never reads your files or calls the network. Keep this folder, then add the companion to your MCP client: `uvx quiet-file-team-mcp`. Product page: [Quiet File Team MCP](../quiet-file-team-mcp/).
- **Setup kit generator** — paid Apify Actor, charged per successfully generated kit; the list rate is on the Apify Tools card and on [pricing.md](../pricing.md); the Store page is authoritative. On the Actor page fill Roster (`TEAM_IDS`, e.g. `lead builder helper`), IANA time zone (`TEAM_TZ`) and Coordinator (`lead`), set the maximum run charge to at least the price shown on the Store page, then Start. Download `OUTPUT.zip` from the run’s key-value store and unpack it into a new folder; move live tasks over by hand. [Open Apify Store](https://apify.com/pandadad0214/quiet-file-team-setup)
- **Quiet File Team Setup Kit** — paid Agensi skill, one-time price on the live listing. Keep this folder, load the skill in your agent, apply the rule packs you want, practice in a new folder and finish the acceptance checklist. Do not replace operational logs with examples. [Open Agensi](https://agensi.io/skills/quiet-file-team-setup-kit)
- **Paid → free** — keep your scripts, drop the optional kit rules and continue with the free README on this page. For a clean copy, clone the GitHub repository separately, back up current data and re-enter active tasks deliberately; never merge `.seen` cursors blindly.

## FAQ

### Is this a hosted service?

No. It is a local Bash kit on one shared Linux machine. There is no server, chat bus or LLM inside, and it makes no network or model calls.

### How do idle routines stop spending tokens?

Start every routine with `has-work.sh <id>`. When it prints exactly `NO WORK`, the routine should stop: no chat, no status, no board line. These are operating practices, not a measured savings promise.

### What does a bot need besides the scripts?

Give each bot the core rules from the repo and paste the early-exit block into each routine, replacing the id and path. Ensure the routine really stops on exactly `NO WORK`.

### Can I put secrets or personal data in the files?

No. The bus is plain files on one trusted machine, with no encryption or access control. Text is checked for long digit strings and email-shaped content as a rough guardrail, not a secret detector. Never put private data in this bus.

### Does the free MCP install the scripts for me?

No. [Quiet File Team MCP](../quiet-file-team-mcp/) explains, configures and checks a team from supplied inputs. Install the Bash core from this page or GitHub, then add the MCP companion if you want setup guidance.
